positions.frame: When the calibration facts are carried forward as structured field-labels rather than as the speaker's own words, whose authority stands behind the restated claim?
positions.why: Both expressions take the calibration facts Quill Ashgrove asserted directly (src-1) and recast them as flat field-label entries under a single shared footing case (fc-1): animator and author fixed to Xena ExpertGH, principal left null. placements.why: The repo's strata is empty, and this envelope's entire content — bringing the Kestrelwood spectrograph to a verified operating frequency and confirming it against named reference plates — is calibration-grain organizational content: it names an instrument-readiness record, not a strategy, product, or architecture claim. Nothing in the (empty) supplied strata covers it, and the envelope's own note ('Observatory Calibration: Kestrelwood Spectrograph') names exactly this category, so it is minted standalone with no forced parent.

placements.why: All three segments carry the same recurring thematic content: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration at 88.4 MHz is not just stated but checked against a named external standard (the June reference plates) and found to hold across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, later re-verifications, drift checks) would keep feeding — the grain test's 'true beyond the words it describes' — rather than a single unrepeatable fact, so it earns its own leaf rather than being folded as raw evidence into something else. src-1 carries Quill's direct assertion of the theme; src-2 and src-3 restate the same theme as structured field-labels, differing only in footing, not in topic, so all three ground the same leaf.
